title: Cardiac CT
description: This page introduces the fundamentals of cardiac CT, including prospective and retrospective gating, temporal resolution and radiation-dose considerations.

sections.title: Cardiac Gating Techniques
sections.description: Cardiac CT requires special gating techniques to reduce the artifacts caused by cardiac motion.
sections.content: The heart is a constantly moving organ, which makes CT imaging challenging. To obtain sharp images of the heart, special gating techniques are needed to reduce motion artifacts. There are two main gating techniques: prospective gating and retrospective gating.
keyPoints: Prospective gating acquires data at a predicted phase of the cardiac cycle (usually mid-diastole)
Retrospective gating acquires data continuously throughout the cardiac cycle and then selects the best phase at reconstruction
Prospective gating delivers a lower radiation dose but works less well in patients with an irregular heart rate
Retrospective gating allows assessment of cardiac function but delivers a higher radiation dose

sections.title: Temporal Resolution
sections.description: Temporal resolution is the ability of a CT scanner to capture a sharp image of a moving object, and it is especially important for cardiac imaging.
sections.content: Temporal resolution is the ability of a CT scanner to capture a sharp image of a moving object. For cardiac imaging, high temporal resolution is essential because the heart is constantly moving. Temporal resolution depends mainly on the rotation time (the time the X-ray tube takes to make one full revolution around the patient). Modern cardiac CT scanners typically have rotation times of 0.28–0.35 s. With partial-scan (half-scan) reconstruction, however, the effective temporal resolution can be improved to about half the rotation time.
keyPoints: Temporal resolution is essential for cardiac imaging
Rotation time is the main factor determining temporal resolution
Partial-scan reconstruction improves the effective temporal resolution
Dual-source CT scanners improve temporal resolution further by using two X-ray tubes

sections.title: Radiation Dose
sections.description: The radiation dose of a cardiac CT scan depends on several factors, including the gating technique, scan range and patient characteristics.
sections.content: The radiation dose of a cardiac CT scan depends on several factors, including the gating technique, the scan range and patient characteristics. Retrospective gating typically delivers 3–4 times the radiation dose of prospective gating because it acquires data continuously throughout the cardiac cycle. Modern CT scanners, however, use several techniques to reduce the dose, including ECG modulation (reducing the tube current during specific phases of the cardiac cycle), iterative reconstruction and low-kV imaging.
keyPoints: The radiation dose of retrospective gating is typically 3–4 times that of prospective gating
ECG modulation reduces the tube current during the non-critical phases of the cardiac cycle, lowering the radiation dose
Iterative reconstruction and low-kV imaging can reduce the radiation dose further
Patient characteristics (such as body habitus) also affect the radiation dose

sections.title: Clinical Applications
sections.description: Cardiac CT has important applications in many clinical settings, including assessment of coronary artery disease, structural heart disease and pre-procedural planning.
sections.content: Cardiac CT has important applications in many clinical settings. The most common is the assessment of coronary artery disease, particularly in patients at intermediate pre-test risk. Cardiac CT can also be used to evaluate cardiac structures (such as the heart valves, atria and ventricles), congenital heart disease and cardiac tumors. It also plays an important role in pre-procedural planning (for example transcatheter aortic valve replacement and coronary artery bypass grafting).
keyPoints: Assessment of coronary artery disease is the most common application of cardiac CT
Cardiac CT can be used to evaluate cardiac structures and congenital heart disease
Cardiac CT plays an important role in pre-procedural planning
Its high negative predictive value makes cardiac CT an effective tool for ruling out coronary artery disease
